writeup.headline: Tenable rates Buy on strong price trend, solid balance sheet and a raised outlook, but sits near Hold.
writeup.thesis: Tenable scores 67, just 3 points above the Hold line, so the Buy rating rests on a narrow margin. The strongest supports are the price trend (score 93), with the price at its 52-week high and shares 117.8 pp ahead of SPY over the last 126 trading days, and the balance sheet (score 86), with net debt only 0.21 times free cash flow. Quality scores 67: the gross margin is 78.0% and the FCF margin is 25.3%, but the operating margin is thin at 3.6% and stock-based pay equals 17.2% of revenue, partly offset by the diluted share count down 6.0% year on year. Growth (51) and valuation (51) hold the score back. Growth runs at TTM revenue growth of 9.9%, and growth slowed by 1.0 pp from the previous quarter. On valuation, P/S of 5.1x and P/FCF of 20.3x are moderate in absolute terms, EV/EBIT of 146.0x is high in absolute terms, and the FCF yield is level with the 10-year Treasury yield. Against its own history the stock is cheap, with P/S cheaper than at 41 of the last 61 month-ends (EV/EBIT not comparable). News is supportive (74): the company beat its Q3 guide and raised its full-year 2026 outlook.
key_risks: Growth is slowing, with latest-quarter revenue growth of 8.6% year on year and growth down 1.0 pp from the prior quarter.
Thin GAAP profitability: an operating margin of 3.6% and EV/EBIT of 146.0x, with stock-based pay at 17.2% of revenue.
After a sharp run the price is 30.4% above its 50-day average and 71.1% above its 200-day average, so a pullback could weaken the trend score.
Q4 revenue guidance of $277.0 million to $280.0 million is roughly flat with Q3 levels, and analyst consensus remains Hold.
what_would_change: A drop of just 3 points would move the rating to Hold, for example if the trend score fades after the rally or growth keeps slowing.
Moving up to Strong Buy needs 13 more points, most plausibly from re-accelerating revenue growth lifting the growth score, or from a better valuation score.
Wider operating margins or lower stock-based pay would lift the quality score.
Negative news, such as a guidance cut or competitive setbacks in exposure management, would pull down the news risk score.
